clue.text: Giddy, similar having struck head

indicators.note: striking off the head of a word knocks away its opening letter

blocks.note: things that are similar are related

explanation.surface: Someone feeling dizzy after taking a similar knock to the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Being giddy with joy is a state of high excitement, close in sense to being thrilled.

clue.text: Best lap

blocks.note: first meaning: to beat or defeat someone, as a verb
second meaning: to drink with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a racing phrase about the fastest circuit, but both words are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: To lick an opponent is informal for thrashing them, and to lick milk is to take it up with the tongue.

clue.text: Body part raised, black in colour

indicators.note: these letters sit inside the colour word, held within it

blocks.note: something raised is high up
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
a tone is a shade or colour

explanation.surface: A bruised limb lifted up, turning black and blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur, the long bone of the upper leg, is a part of the body's skeleton.

clue.text: Romantic novel read well!

indicators.note: something novel is new, so the word read is put into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
both are exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A reader gushing about a love story that is a good read.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic and idealised, as in a person lost in pleasant reverie, or an attractive heart-throb.

clue.text: Serious film about a double Dutch lover?

indicators.note: the serious film is wrapped about a single letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: a serious problem is a big one
a thin film of moisture
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weighty film about a Dutchman who speaks gibberish while courting.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch is Cockney slang for wife (from 'duchess'), so a double Dutch lover has two wives; 'double Dutch' as gibberish is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who marries a second wife while still married to the first commits bigamy, loving two spouses.

clue.text: Where plants studied in old forest on which log cabin built, housing much appreciated

indicators.note: a cabin that is built is assembled from parts, so its letters are put together afresh
the cabin letters house the thanks word, holding it inside before rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
ta is British informal thanks
the Forest of Arden, the ancient woodland of Warwickshire and As You Like It

explanation.surface: A log cabin set up in an ancient forest, where some grateful botanist does fieldwork.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the rebuilt cabin sits on top of the forest, hence 'on which'.
explanation.definitionFit: A public garden where plants are grown for scientific study and display, such as Kew.

clue.text: Powdery on the moon, scrap’s gathered up

indicators.note: a scrap that has gathered something holds it within itself
in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: lunar means of or on the moon
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: Moon dust described as powdery, with a scrap of it collected by an astronaut.
explanation.definitionFit: Granular material consists of small grains, so it is close in texture to a powder.

clue.text: He painted Earthling and Venutian, say

blocks.note: a human being, a person of Earth
ET is an extraterrestrial, as a being from Venus would be

explanation.surface: An artist portraying both a human and a creature from Venus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the Venutian as only an example of an alien.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was the French painter of Olympia and Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe.

clue.text: The other pieces for old band

blocks.note: 'the other' is a coy British euphemism for sex
pieces is slang for guns

explanation.surface: Bits of something else set aside for a former group.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1970s British punk group fronted by Johnny Rotten, now long disbanded.

clue.text: One Direction’s corrosive agent on the radio?

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is received by sound alone, not spelling

blocks.note: an oxidant is a substance that causes corrosion such as rust

explanation.surface: A boy band's caustic influence being discussed on a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction looks like the boy band, but it is simply one compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occident is the West, which is one of the four compass points.

clue.text: Girl, cross with deadline, finally gets extension

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: a girl's name
a cross is the letter shape
the last letter of deadline

explanation.surface: An angry girl, up against a deadline, at last wins more time.
explanation.walkthrough: Extension looks like more time for the deadline, but it is a building.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extra wing or building added on to the main one, a building extension.

clue.text: Garbage in tum, husband – one of those?

definitions.text: Garbage in tum, husband – one of those?

indicators.note: garbage is rubbish, so the following letters are a jumbled mess

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A wife eyeing her husband, his belly full of junk, and wondering if he is one of those types.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the fodder and a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who will eat anything, leftovers included, is jokingly called this, as if a rubbish bin.

clue.text: Local call outlining prophecy

indicators.note: to outline something is to draw around it, so one word surrounds another

blocks.note: to dial is to call on the phone
a prophetic vision of the future

explanation.surface: A phone call to a local number outlining a prediction.
explanation.definitionFit: A divisional office serves one region or division, so it is regional or local in scope.

clue.text: Somewhere for swimming cap, one’s head!

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a lid caps a container
first letter of one

explanation.surface: A swimming cap is somewhere for one's head at the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is an open-air public swimming pool, a place for swimming.

clue.text: Virtue in large settlement, hurrying to bank when last one divorced!

indicators.note: the final letter is split off, divorced from the rest
banks line a river on both sides, so the settlement flanks what goes inside

blocks.note: hurrying is acting in haste
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A city dweller rushing to the bank after a divorce, virtue lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastity, abstaining from sex, is traditionally counted as one of the seven heavenly virtues.

clue.text: I don’t want to listen – but a labourer might?

blocks.note: surface reading: a dismissive retort, holding up a palm to silence someone
setter's reading: a labourer is a farm or factory worker, so speaking to one is literally addressing a worker

explanation.walkthrough: A hand is a manual worker, so the brush-off phrase is literally what you do to address one.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang retort tells someone you are refusing to listen to them, often with a raised palm.

clue.text: A generic kind of philanthropist or self-help guru

indicators.note: a kind of something is a variant form, so the letters appear in a different version

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A rather ordinary sort of benefactor or motivational author.
explanation.walkthrough: Two famous bearers of the surname fit: Andrew, the steel magnate who funded libraries, and Dale, author of How to Win Friends and Influence People.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Carnegie gave away a fortune, and Dale Carnegie wrote the classic self-improvement book.

clue.text: Stumble across wrong wire in security device

indicators.note: a wrong arrangement is an incorrect one, so the letters are muddled
the stumble lies across the other word, spanning it on either side

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
to stumble is to fall

explanation.surface: An electrician tripping over a miswired alarm system.
explanation.definitionFit: A firewall is a network security system that blocks unauthorised traffic, protecting a computer.

clue.text: Bloomer in cunning manner initially erased

indicators.note: the initial letter is rubbed out, leaving the rest

blocks.note: slily is a spelling of slyly, meaning cunningly

explanation.surface: A blunder slyly covered up from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer here is not a mistake but something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily is a flowering plant, and a flower is jokingly called a bloomer in crosswords.

clue.text: Legend written below canopy of pine, part of trunk

indicators.note: a canopy is the top of a tree, and in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter
in a down entry, a word placed below another follows it

blocks.note: the opening letter of pine
Elvis Presley, a rock'n'roll legend

explanation.surface: A legend carved into a tree beneath the pine canopy, part way up its trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Trunk is the tree's surface sense; here it is the human torso.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelvis is the bony basin at the base of the torso, the body's trunk.

clue.text: Is that concealed by instrumental entertainer?

definitions.text: Is that concealed by instrumental entertainer?

blocks.clueFragment: Is that concealed by instrumental entertainer?
blocks.note: surface reading: does a musician keep some secret gift under wraps
setter's reading: a word for gift or ability sits inside these two words, straddling the gap

explanation.walkthrough: TALENT runs across instrumenTAL ENTertainer, so the phrase literally describes itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An unrecognised gift or skill that a person possesses but keeps out of view.

clue.text: Doctor you and I had, healer

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
U is text-speak for you
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A patient recalling a physician the two of them once shared.
explanation.definitionFit: Druids were Celtic priests who also acted as healers and wise men, practising herbal medicine.

clue.text: See 15
Not appreciated – as a number made redundant?

blocks.note: first meaning: uncelebrated, without recognition
second meaning, playful: a song that was dropped and never performed

explanation.surface: A worker laid off, feeling their efforts went unrecognised.
explanation.walkthrough: A number is a song here, not a figure or employee.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsung hero is one whose deeds go uncelebrated, and literally a song never performed.

clue.text: Turkey probed by animal doctor, alas, some leave

indicators.note: something probed has an instrument pushed inside it

blocks.note: a turkey is a flop or failure
a vet treats animals
ay is an old cry of woe

explanation.surface: A vet examining a turkey, sadly, while some staff are away.
explanation.walkthrough: A duvet day is a day off taken at short notice to stay in bed, a British coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a single day of leave from work, taken when one cannot face going in.

clue.text: Reassembly of gun, doable after unloading a weapon

indicators.note: reassembling a gun means putting its parts back in a new order
unloading something takes it out, removing it from the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: Putting a gun back together is doable once it is unloaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a heavy club, a blunt weapon used for striking.

clue.text: Before year, second went fast

indicators.note: placed before means these letters come ahead of the year abbreviation

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
went is informal for urinated
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A year ago, someone left in a moment, rushing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' is the toilet sense of going; 'fast' is the definition, not part of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedy and fast both mean moving at great pace, as synonymous adjectives.
